title: Window Tally Chart
subject: math
learningGoal: Collect data with tally marks and read it to answer a question.
realWorldHook: Town planners count cars and bikes to decide where to build roads and bike lanes.

materials.householdSubstitution: A whiteboard or the back of an envelope

materials.item: A window or doorway with a view
materials.householdSubstitution: A picture book with lots of things to count

noPurchaseRoute: Any window, or a busy picture in a book you own.
parentPreview: Your child counts what passes by (cars, people, birds) for a few minutes using tally marks, then reads the chart to answer 'which was most?'

parent.parentSays: What do you think goes past our window most: cars, people or birds?

child.screen: What goes past your window the most?
child.readAloudText: What goes past your window the most?

parent.parentSays: Let's make three columns and draw a line every time we see one. Every fifth line crosses the other four.
parent.whyThisWorks: Tally marks in fives make counting quicker, just like counting in fives.

child.screen: Make a tally mark for each one you see!
child.readAloudText: Make a tally mark for each one. Cross the fifth one.

parent.parentSays: Count each column. Count the bundles of five first.

child.screen: How many cars did you count?
child.readAloudText: How many cars did you count?

parent.parentSays: Which column has the most? How many more than the smallest?
Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
Was your first guess right? What else could we count?

misconceptions.signal: Draws the fifth mark as a separate line, or crosses after four.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: How many lines are in one bundle, counting the crossing line?

misconceptions.signal: Picks the column that looks longest even though bundles are uneven.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: Let's count each column instead of looking. Which number is biggest?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Two bundles of five and three more marks. How many?

interpretation.partial: Counts each line one by one.

child.screen: Two bundles of 5 and 3 more. How many?
child.readAloudText: Two bundles of five and three more. How many?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: If we want to know our family's favourite fruit, how could we find out?

child.screen: How could you find your family's favourite fruit?
child.readAloudText: How could you find your family's favourite fruit? Tell your grown-up.

extension: Turn the tally into a bar chart with one square per item.

shorterVersion.description: Tally one thing for two minutes.

accessibilityAdaptations: Use stickers or counters instead of drawing tally marks.
Choose a slower scene (a picture book) if the street is too fast.
